started_at.description: WO-010-R7-R1: must be at or before completed_at. format: date-time is an annotation the installed jsonschema/FormatChecker does not assert, so a malformed or inverted interval is caught semantically by analysis.provenance.collection_run_problems, not by this schema alone.

completed_at.description: WO-010-R7-R1: must be at or after started_at. See started_at's description for why this is enforced semantically, not just by format.

request_url.description: The URL this adapter built and requested. May differ from response_url if the source redirected.

response_url.description: The final, redirect-resolved URL the response actually came from (HttpResponse.url). Distinct from request_url so a redirect that changes host/path is visible and auditable, not silently discarded.

content_type.description: The response's Content-Type header, verbatim (including any parameters, e.g. '; charset=utf-8'), after collectors.http_client.validate_content_type has checked it against the source's allowlist. Null when the header was absent or the run never reached a response (e.g. dry_run).

records_emitted.description: WO-010-R7-R1: one documented count convention per status, enforced structurally below and semantically by analysis.provenance.collection_run_problems. 'success': a non-null integer equal to len(emitted_records) -- 0 for a genuine zero-output run, which still produces and hashes an empty manifest. 'not_modified': exactly 0. 'error'/'disabled'/'dry_run': null, never 0 -- these statuses never produce a manifest at all, which is a different fact from a success run's manifest legitimately containing zero records.

emitted_records.description: WO-010-R6 §1, made universally present WO-010-R7-R1. The deterministic output manifest: exactly the records this run actually emitted. A 'success' run's records_emitted count must equal the length of this list; a 'not_modified' run must leave this empty and instead set supersedes_run_id. Always present (WO-010-R7-R1 adds it to the top-level required list); null for the statuses that never emit (disabled/error/dry_run).

output_manifest_sha256.description: WO-010-R6 §1. Deterministic hash over emitted_records (canonical: sorted by record_id, JSON-encoded with sort_keys). Null when emitted_records is null.

supersedes_run_id.description: WO-010-R6 §1, tightened WO-010-R7 §1. For a 'not_modified' run: the prior run whose emitted_records remain current (required, non-null, for 'not_modified'; must be null for every other status). A not_modified run never claims new records of its own; acquisition-binding checks follow this chain to find a record's governing manifest.

allOf.description: WO-010-R7 §1, tightened WO-010-R7-R1: a 'success' run must carry a complete output manifest -- emitted_records is a non-null array (an empty array is how a successful zero-output run is expressed), records_emitted is a non-null integer equal to len(emitted_records) (checked exactly by analysis.provenance.collection_run_problems, since JSON Schema cannot cross-reference an array's length), output_manifest_sha256 is a non-null hash of it, and it supersedes nothing.

WO-010-R7 §1, tightened WO-010-R7-R1: a 'not_modified' run claims no records of its own -- emitted_records is exactly the empty array, never null and never populated, records_emitted is exactly 0 (never null, never positive) -- carries no output-manifest hash of its own (the governing hash lives on the successful run supersedes_run_id points to), and must name that prior run.

WO-010-R7 §1, tightened WO-010-R7-R1: 'error', 'disabled' and 'dry_run' runs emitted nothing -- no output manifest, no manifest hash, no supersession, and records_emitted is null (never 0: a null count means no manifest was ever produced, which is a different fact from a success run's manifest legitimately being empty) -- so no record may ever bind to one.
